title: P4 · Scanned and checked
description: Nurse Reem scans the code in the facility's EMR and enters the passcode. The EMR checks the signature with Malaysia's public key, fetched from GDHCN: the record really comes from Malaysia's HIE and has not been changed. Step 4 and step B of the overview of key process flows.

illustrationStyle.prompt: Warm, flat digital illustration with soft shading and clean outlines, friendly and respectful, in the style of a public-health storybook. Wide banner, aspect ratio 11:4. Bright natural daylight, soft pastel palette with clear colour accents. Faces in gentle three-quarter view with expressive, kind features. Technology shown as simple, oversized icons: a phone with a QR code, a shield with a check mark, a small speech bubble with a symbol. No readable text, no logos, no real brands, no flags with text. All people are fictional.

cast.description: Malaysian man, 61, slim, short grey hair, kind face. Batik shirt in Malaysia. In KSA, white two-piece ihram (unstitched towelling cloth, right shoulder bare when in ihram), a small waist pouch and one phone.
His wife, about 58. White modest Hajj outfit and white telekung-style hijab in KSA; pastel baju kurung and tudung in Malaysia.
Saudi nurse, 30s, navy scrubs, white headscarf.

notes: Ihram (two white unstitched sheets) is for men only; women wear ordinary modest clothing, usually white, face and hands uncovered.
Keep the Kaaba and other holy sites far in the background or out of frame.
Keep medical signs text-free so generators don't invent wrong Arabic.
The picture carries no text: the step title and the caption are page text.

steps.title: Scanned and checked
steps.headline: Nurse Reem scans the code and enters the passcode; the EMR checks the signature with Malaysia's key from GDHCN.
steps.touchpoint: Facility EMR with bar code scanner
steps.narrative: Nurse Reem scans the code in the facility's EMR and enters the passcode. The EMR checks the signature with Malaysia's public key, fetched from GDHCN: the record really comes from Malaysia's HIE and has not been changed. Step 4 and step B of the overview of key process flows.

experiences.doing: Scans the QR code into the EMR and enters the passcode; sees the signature verified.
Sits and waits while the code is scanned.

experiences.feeling: “They knew what to do with it.”

experiences.doing: Decodes the QR code and verifies its signature with Malaysia's public key.

steps.painPoint: Without a signature check, the clinic cannot tell a genuine record from a forged or altered one.
steps.enabler: The EMR verifies the signature against a key it got from the trust network, with no call to Malaysia needed.
steps.policy: What protection should the passcode give — and is a passcode shared by every pilgrim of a country a passcode at all?
gaps: Not yet consistent: the concepts page says the default passcode is the pilgrim's birth date; the Malaysian implementation sets one standard passcode for all its pilgrims for the season.
The Clinical Encounter for Unplanned Care diagram draws no separate task for entering the passcode.

references.label: Business process: Clinical Encounter for Unplanned Care (scan QR code, add passcode, verify QR code signature)
